name: VARoleArbiterWhatsappHealthClaim

custom.system_prompt: Bex received a forwarded health claim from a relative, alarmed about a common household item. Griff thinks it sounds like classic forwarded-message exaggeration. They ask Sigma to help assess the claim and its source rather than just react to it.

assistant.name: Sigma
assistant.tts_prompt: Neutral, calm, doesn't dismiss family members' concern

sound_effects_config.prompt: Living room, evening, phone buzzing on the table

initial_prompt: Generate a scene where Bex receives a forwarded message from a relative warning about a common household item, worded urgently and dramatically. Bex is a little alarmed; Griff immediately suspects it's an exaggerated forward rather than something to worry about, based on how it's written. They ask Sigma to assess the claim and whether it has the hallmarks of misinformation. Keep every line short and natural.

user1.name: Bex
user1.tts_prompt: A little alarmed, wants to be careful

variations.context: Couple assessing a forwarded family health-warning message

setting.relationship_dynamic: Bex takes family concern seriously by default; Griff has seen this exact pattern of forward before
setting.background: The message uses urgent, alarmist language and cites no actual source
setting.conversation_style: Short, Bex a little worried, Griff recognizing a familiar shape of misinformation

scenario_template.topic: Bex reads the alarming message aloud, worried; Griff immediately flags that it reads like a classic exaggerated forward, citing the tone and lack of sourcing. A few short exchanges — Bex not wanting to just dismiss family concern.
scenario_template.note: Bex shouldn't be dismissed outright for taking it seriously.

scenario_template.topic: Bex asks Sigma to check whether the claim actually holds up rather than just trusting Griff's instinct or dismissing her own concern, addressing Sigma directly in one short line.
scenario_template.mood: Wanting to be careful, not dismissive
scenario_template.note: e.g. 'Sigma, can you check if there's anything to this?'

scenario_template.topic: Sigma assesses the claim itself and notes the hallmarks that suggest exaggeration or lack of sourcing — urgent tone, no attributable source, common forwarded-message pattern — without mocking the concern or the relative who sent it. One or two short sentences.
scenario_template.note: Sigma explains why this pattern is a red flag, not just that it is one.

scenario_template.topic: Bex is relieved but says she'll gently let the relative know rather than ignoring it outright; Griff is satisfied but doesn't gloat about calling it. Keep this realistic and warm toward the family member who sent it.
scenario_template.mood: Relieved, practical, not dismissive of the sender
scenario_template.note: Avoid mocking the relative who forwarded it.

scenario_template.topic: They agree on how Bex will respond to the relative, one short line each.

variations.context: Friends debating a forwarded app security warning

setting.relationship_dynamic: one of them takes family concern seriously by default; one of them has seen this exact pattern of forward before
setting.background: A friend shares a warning about a widely-used mobile app
setting.conversation_style: Short, one of them a little worried, one of them recognizing a familiar shape of misinformation

scenario_template.topic: One reads aloud a warning message about app privacy risks; the other suggests it's probably sensationalized due to its style and lack of cited evidence.
scenario_template.note: Highlight contrasting reactions: concern versus pattern recognition.

scenario_template.topic: One asks Sigma to verify whether the app warning is credible, wanting a neutral opinion.
scenario_template.note: Request to Sigma should feel natural and brief.

scenario_template.topic: Sigma evaluates the claim, noting the dramatic tone and absence of credible sources.
scenario_template.note: Focus on the reasonable evaluation without dismissing the message entirely.

scenario_template.topic: One feels reassured and plans to explain their findings to the friend who shared it, others satisfied with the clarification.
scenario_template.note: Show a thoughtful and friendly response.

scenario_template.topic: They agree how to update the friend who sent the warning, keeping it light.

user1.name: Yue
user1.tts_prompt: A little alarmed, wants to be careful

variations.context: Neighbors evaluating a forwarded grocery item scare

setting.mood: Mild concern with a dash of doubt
setting.relationship_dynamic: one of them takes family concern seriously by default; one of them has seen this exact pattern of forward before
setting.background: A neighbor forwards an alert about a popular grocery item
setting.conversation_style: Short, one of them a little worried, one of them recognizing a familiar shape of misinformation

scenario_template.topic: One reads a worrying message about a grocery item being unsafe; the other doubts its validity, pointing out the message's vague claims.
One suggests checking with Sigma to ensure the warning is not just a rumor.
scenario_template.note: Sigma should be addressed naturally and simply.

scenario_template.topic: Sigma analyzes the warning, mentioning its vague assertions and lack of expert backing.
One relaxes after the analysis and decides to discuss it with the neighbor calmly; the other is glad to have checked.
They conclude on the best way to inform the neighbor amicably.
scenario_template.note: Conclude on a gentle and amicable note.

user1.name: Ines
user1.tts_prompt: A little alarmed, wants to be careful

user1.name: Bex
user1.role: Quick, curious graphic designer, takes family concern seriously even when the message sounds alarmist. Speaks in short sentences. Relieved by a credibility check but stays kind toward the relative who sent it.

user2.name: Griff
user2.role: Grounded electrician, recognizes the shape of an exaggerated forwarded message quickly. Speaks in short sentences. Satisfied when confirmed right but doesn't gloat about it.

assistant.name: Sigma
assistant.role: Arbiter. Assesses a forwarded claim for hallmarks of exaggeration or misinformation — tone, sourcing, pattern — and explains why, respectfully and without mocking the concern or the person who forwarded it.

conversation_structure: This is a source-credibility case about a forwarded family message, not a simple fact-check
Sigma names the specific hallmarks that suggest exaggeration (tone, lack of sourcing) rather than a vague dismissal
Sigma and both partners stay respectful toward the relative who sent the message
Every line is one or two short spoken sentences
The resolution is warm and practical — the concerned partner still plans a kind response, not just dismissal
assistant_behavior: Sigma explains why the message shows signs of exaggeration, specifically
Sigma never mocks the sender or the person who raised the concern
